test_bundle_gates.py::TheInstallIsAskedA.why: TWO WALKS OF ONE FOLDER. The write rule's scope walked the bundle with its own skip list while the checker's walk had learned that a tool's signed cache is not a shipped file.

retired.why: The runner is now read at the one door every escape passes through: bundle_shell.every_command_is asks again what a wrapper hands on before runs_a_rule_tool is ever asked, so reading the first word as the program inside runs_a_rule_tool can no longer refuse the wrapped rule tool. The door's own plants (AnEscapeIsAskedOfEveryCommand) hold that reading now; the elsewhere and evasion plants here still redden.

test_bundle_action.py::ACommandsWriteIsJ.why: THE READING AS IT WAS: the first word is the program, so `timeout 3000 python -B tools/dev/plants.py add x.json` - a record re-measured the way a held change says it may be - was refused as if it built on the change.

single_site.test_bundle.py::EveryHookMustBeIMPORTABL: Both of its tests are about one property of one folder - that importing a hook does nothing - and the derivation already walks every `guard_*.py`, so a hook added tomorrow is covered without a second plant. The instance plant restores the bare `main()` that shipped, which is the state this class was written against.
